To automatically start your machine, you must use the Wake On Lan method.

You must enable the feature in the BIOS, and also in the Windows Device Manager.

RomMonitor monitors disk space and the SMART health of your drives.
An alert email is sent in the event of a critical SMART failure.
A log is maintained for every detected issue.

A web page allows this information to be viewed remotely.

Net.OriginExplanation: Origin is information independent of severity. It explains WHO this IP is.
Net.PatternExplanation: This does NOT change the severity of the IP shown above. It adds a global rule in NetMonitor.config. Future alerts matching this pattern will be classified in the chosen list.
Net.BeaconingHelp: Detects regular malware communications to a command-and-control server (C2). Spyware often sends a request every X seconds. The higher the jitter, the stricter the detection.
Net.CrawlerHelp: Generic crawlers (Yandex, Baidu, Infrawatch...). Matching IPs will be marked Crawler (dark blue) and blocked if the option is enabled.
Net.IgnoredNetworksHelp: Ignored networks (CIDR): these addresses will never trigger an alert. Useful for loopback and local networks.
Net.PatternsHelp: Define here the patterns that determine the label (Safe, Critical, Scanner, Crawler) assigned to an IP. These lists are compared against the ISP, Org or reverse DNS.
Net.ScannerHelp: Legitimate research scanners (Shodan, Censys, Palo Alto...). Matching IPs will be marked Trusted (yellow) and blocked if the option is enabled.
Net.TrustedDevicesHelp: These devices can connect to the Web without OTP. They are remembered for 30 days. Revoking a device forces it to go through OTP again on its next connection.
Net.WebHelp: Allows viewing alerts from a web browser (localhost or local network). Disable it if you do not use this interface.
Net.WhitelistHelp: Removing a process makes it reappear in the 'Pending processes' table at the next network event. Unchecking 'Active' temporarily disables trust without deleting the entry.
Email.Aide: You must enter your sending information and a recipient so that the other features of the software can send reports automatically.
Media.Description: MediaMonitor tells you which media are currently playing or have been played. The process can be automated according to the machine activity period. A report can be sent automatically before shutdown or manually from the interface.
Sys.Description: SystemMonitor monitors CPU, memory, graphics cards and network usage. A web page lets you check this information remotely. Data is collected by a Windows service.
OnOff.Info: Schedule shutdown or sleep for your machine. Automatic startup relies on Wake-on-LAN.
Stop.Hint: Automation installs two tasks: one at machine shutdown, one at startup.

Rom.Info: RomMonitor monitors disk space and the SMART health of your drives. On a critical SMART failure, an alert email is sent. A log is kept up to date for every problem detected.
Wake.Info: WakeMonitor can report information about what woke your machine. This information is sent by email. You can create a scheduled task that reacts to Power-Troubleshooter with ID = 1.
